transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
My sleep has gotten really messed up. I’ll stay up half the night with my mind running, or I wake up way too early and feel like I never really rested.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or like you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah. Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling. Even being in my condo, which I worked really hard for, can just make me want to cry.
How many weeks or months has this heavy, empty feeling along with the sleep trouble been going on?
About five months, I think. It was there before, but it got a lot worse after I bought the condo.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or relationships—more days than not, and having trouble controlling that worry?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been feeling low, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying about lots of different things.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even ones unrelated to the condo, over these past several months?
Yeah. I stopped going to salsa class, and my paints are still sitting out on the table. I look at them and just feel nothing, like they belong to somebody else.
Over these past several months, have you noticed a drop in your energy level or difficulty concentrating on tasks, even simple ones?
Yeah. Even if I’ve been in bed all night, walking from the parking lot into the office feels like I’m dragging sandbags. By lunchtime my brain just feels worn out.
Over these past several months, have you found yourself feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or overly critical of yourself?
Yeah. I keep telling myself I was stupid to take on the mortgage, and that I’ve let everyone down. Even though, objectively, none of the bills are late.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports approximately 5 months of depressed/empty mood, anhedonia (loss of interest in salsa dancing and painting), sleep disturbance (initial and early morning awakening), fatigue/low energy, and feelings of worthlessness/excessive guilt. These core depressive symptoms co-occur and represent a change from prior functioning, with functional impairment (withdrawal from valued activities, difficulty at work) and a clear psychosocial stressor (purchase of condo/financial strain) preceding symptom worsening. Excessive, uncontrollable worry across multiple domains was explicitly denied, making Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) less likely. No history of chronic (>2 year) low-grade symptoms was elicited to support Persistent Depressive Disorder (F34.1), and no manic/hypomanic symptoms, psychotic features, or specific precipitating bereavement/trauma were reported. Given the symptom cluster meets depressive episode criteria but insufficient detail was gathered on all 9 DSM-like symptoms (e.g., appetite/weight change, psychomotor changes, suicidality) to specify severity or recurrence, Major Depressive Disorder, unspecified (F32.9) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
